report.headline: Cowboys keep the lid on a sputtering Buccaneers attack
report.openingParagraph: Buccaneers at Cowboys, 8:15 PM ET at AT&T Stadium on Prime Video, roof open, 80 degrees, rain chance 0%. The Buccaneers are 0-4, the Cowboys are 2-2, and both sides are on four days of rest. Two pass-first offenses, 67% pass rate each, point to more possessions and more variance. The model projects Cowboys by 6.9, 70% to win, Buccaneers 20 to Cowboys 27, confidence high.

sections.title: The throw game against the home secondary
paragraphs: This is the matchup that shapes the game plan. The Cowboys rank No. 32 of 32 in pass success allowed at 61%, which should be a gift. It is not. The Buccaneers rank No. 28 in pass success at 39% and No. 27 in pass explosiveness at 1.18, while the Cowboys sit No. 14 of 32 at limiting explosive passes at 1.29.

That is a clear edge for the defense. The Buccaneers should expect to drive the long way. Caleb Downs plays 97% of defensive snaps as the coverage leader, with 27 tackles and 1 pass defensed. Watch the longest Buccaneers completion. If it is under 25 yards at the half, the Cowboys have won the matchup.

sections.title: Running into a stout front
paragraphs: The second real edge also belongs to a defense. The Buccaneers are No. 5 of 32 against the run at 34% and No. 5 by EPA a carry at -0.22. The Cowboys rank No. 13 in rush success at 43% and No. 12 in EPA a carry at -0.03. Expect more second-and-long than usual. Josiah Trotter, on 86% of defensive snaps with 33 tackles, is the run stopper to track. Under 3 yards per carry in the first quarter and the game plan has to change.

sections.title: The long downs cut the other way
paragraphs: The Buccaneers rank No. 25 of 32 on passing downs at 31%, which is bad. The Cowboys rank No. 32 at 55%, which is worse. A third-and-8 is not a stop here. Two Buccaneers conversions on third-and-long in the first half break the Cowboys plan.

sections.title: Where the numbers land
paragraphs: The market has the Cowboys -8.5, opened -9.5, total 47.5. Model and market agree on the side at about 8.5, and 3 of 4 systems lean Buccaneers against the number, the EdgeSheet model among them. Model total is 45, a lean under by 2.5.

report.oneLineForCard: The Cowboys are No. 32 in pass success allowed, and the Buccaneers still cannot take advantage.
